problem: Existing map/scene-graph ObjectNav methods (SG-Nav, ASCENT) collapse noisy perception into single hard semantic labels, causing illogical map layouts, overconfident LLM decisions and false-positive stops.
motivation: Open-vocabulary navigation suffers from semantic ambiguity and sim-vs-real domain shift in detectors (e.g. sofa mistaken for bed). Discarding the label distribution loses information irreversibly and propagates errors into planning, so uncertainty must be kept and reasoned over, and stops must be verified.
key_idea: Keep full categorical distributions in a hierarchical object-group-room 3D scene graph, sample LLM-pruned plausible 'worlds' to pick landmarks by pairwise LLM comparison, and calibrate goal-stop confidence with a retrieval memory of past successes and failures.
insight: Ablations show the hierarchy is critical: removing Group nodes drops HM3D SR to 58.8, about the same as the deterministic w/o 3D-PSG variant (58.4), because flat joint distributions explode combinatorially. Pairwise comparison beats absolute Ranking (66.1 vs 59.9 SR on HM3D), and more sampled worlds help (K=1 63.3, K=3 66.1). EEC intercepts 76.9% of false-positive stops on a hard subset, and a small memory (10 entries) suffices.
method: 3D-PSG object nodes: per-object vote-count vector normalized into a categorical distribution over classes (instead of Dirichlet updates, since detectors are poorly calibrated)
Hierarchical factorization: objects clustered into groups whose joint configuration probability is the product of member beliefs; room hypotheses aggregate group distributions
Multiverse construction: enumerate top-K_g group and top-K_r room configurations, filter with an LLM for logical conflicts, sample K=3 deterministic worlds

Intrinsic uncertainty-aware exploration: candidate landmarks from Voronoi graph and frontiers, scored by U_gain = alpha*spatial unknown-area coverage (72 rays) + semantic entropy of nearby objects; low-gain landmarks pruned (tau=0.1)
Stochastic pairwise comparison: in each sampled world the LLM compares landmark pairs given the goal; wins are averaged over worlds into S, and l* = argmax(S + 0.5*U_gain)

Evidential Experience Calibrator: positive/negative memory banks store visual embedding plus room-distribution and group-distribution descriptors; S_final = S_det + S_pos - gamma*S_neg (gamma=2), stop only if > delta=0.61
Diversity-driven update: banks (capacity 10) updated after each episode with GT feedback, evicting the entry most similar to the rest

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (frozen LLM reasoner) + GLIP detector + Grounded-SAM segmentation
setting.training_data: none (training-free); the EEC memory is updated online across validation episodes (lifelong protocol)
setting.observation: posed egocentric RGB-D with odometry, 800x800 occupancy map
setting.action_space: discrete MOVE_FORWARD / TURN_LEFT / TURN_RIGHT / LOOK_UP / LOOK_DOWN / STOP, with landmark-level planning and a local controller
setting.privileged: EEC memory updates use ground-truth success/failure feedback at the end of each episode (online lifelong protocol); no GT map or pose otherwise

numbers.extra: EEC memory updated online with GT episode-end feedback across validation episodes; 500-step limit

results: PSG-Nav reaches SR 66.1/44.8/67.9 on HM3D/MP3D/HSSD, beating SG-Nav (54.0 on HM3D) and BeliefMapNav (61.4 on HM3D, 65.2 on HSSD), and slightly above ASCENT (65.4/44.5) in SR but with lower SPL on HM3D and MP3D. The zero-shot variant w/o EEC (63.5/43.3/66.1) already beats most baselines, though ASCENT is higher on HM3D SR.
limitations: Relies on a 2D occupancy map, so it cannot handle stairs or multi-floor navigation (40.2% of failures are geometric)
Repeated LLM pairwise comparisons add latency in large environments
EEC uses GT success/failure feedback for online memory updates, and detector false positives/misses remain (37.5% and 22.3% of failures); real-world results are qualitative only
